# Relational contracts: identity, NULL and outer-join equivalence

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `algorithms-sql-relations` · **Algorithms, Coding & Debugging** · Catalog level: foundation

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S03-Q033](#S03-Q033)

<p>Can a LEFT JOIN query be rewritten using RIGHT JOIN while preserving its result? Explain what must be compared or changed.</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Verify that a schema or join rewrite preserves the declared relational data contract.</p>

<ul>
<li>Distinguish row identity from additional uniqueness requirements.</li>
<li>Specify accepted and rejected nullable-key inputs for the actual database.</li>
<li>Compare the full result of outer-join rewrites, including unmatched and duplicate rows.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>Can a LEFT JOIN report be rewritten with RIGHT JOIN without changing its output? Before comparing results, establish the identities and uniqueness assumptions of the input data. Keys describe permitted data; NULL and unmatched rows expose the boundaries that a rewrite must preserve. The headcount exercise now has its own focused group.</p>

### S03-Q034 · Foundation

<p>Compare a primary key and a unique constraint. How would you choose them for a row identity and another business key?</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q034](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q034)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q034](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q034)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare primary key and unique constraints.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the roles of identity and uniqueness in a schema. Distinguish the logical constraint from implementation details of indexes.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design key constraints from the meaning of the data.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify SQL Server version, nullability and whether keys are composite. Verify documented constraint/index behavior instead of transferring assumptions from another database.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Separates the chosen row identity from other uniqueness requirements.</li>
<li>Uses invalid insert/update examples to test the intended schema contract.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Defining the difference only as clustered versus nonclustered, without discussing identity or nullability.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you model an optional business identifier that must be unique when provided?</li>
</ul>

<a id="S03-Q035"></a>

### S03-Q035 · Mechanism

<p>How do nullable values interact with a uniqueness requirement in your database? Define the expected behavior before choosing a constraint or index.</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q035](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q035)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q035](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q035)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Discuss nullable values and uniqueness semantics.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>A missing value and a duplicate provided value are different business cases. Make the schema&#x27;s accepted and rejected inputs explicit.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Translate an optional-value requirement into testable uniqueness semantics.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Start with SQL Server, its version, single/composite columns and the chosen constraint/index form. Consult official documentation; different database systems must not be assumed equivalent.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Predicts acceptance of several NULL and repeated non-NULL examples within the declared scope.</li>
<li>Tests the selected database mechanism against the intended business rule.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Using a blanket claim about SQL NULL uniqueness without specifying the engine or key form.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What additional cases would you test for a two-column unique key with one nullable column?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S03-Q033"></a>

### S03-Q033 · Application

<p>Can a LEFT JOIN query be rewritten using RIGHT JOIN while preserving its result? Explain what must be compared or changed.</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q033](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q033)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q033](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q033)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain whether a `LEFT JOIN` can be rewritten as a `RIGHT JOIN` and what must change for the result set to remain equivalent.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Equivalence means retaining the same projected rows and values, including unmatched data. Consider the whole query rather than replacing one keyword.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about outer-join equivalence from a concrete data example.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State both input tables, join predicates, filters and selected columns. Row ordering requires an explicit ORDER BY; duplicate rows remain relevant to result equivalence.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Tracks which side&#x27;s unmatched rows must survive and checks null-extended results.</li>
<li>Tests matching, unmatched and duplicate input cases against the full query.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Changing LEFT to RIGHT without examining table positions, column projection or filters.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would a filter on the unmatched side affect your equivalence check?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>Review a data-access refactor that adds uniqueness to an optional customer business code and rewrites an order report from LEFT JOIN to RIGHT JOIN. For the deployed SQL Server version, define allowed insert/update examples and compare projected report rows using customers without orders and duplicate join inputs. State which source assumptions the refactor relies on.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Distinguishes primary/unique roles and compares a simple outer-join example.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>States engine and key scope, tests nullable uniqueness, and proves query equivalence with predicates, projection and row multiplicity retained.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>No declared database behavior or boundary inputs/results are supplied; constraints and equivalent-looking SQL have not been verified.</p>
